_why: PGN-A8: a fixture that already contains the answers makes every stage vacuous.
This file is the ANSWER KEY and it lives OUTSIDE the corpus on purpose. The first draft
carried the same information in `<!-- fixture role: ... -->` comments inside each corpus
file, which DEFEATED R6: the comment in neigong.md named 罡元, so the realm that is
supposed to be un-orderable because no page places it was sitting in the very page it must
be absent from. A `<!-- source: ... is_authored_source = FALSE -->` header leaked the
provenance the pipeline is meant to be tested on, too.
Metadata about a test must never live inside the thing under test. Enforced by

provenance._rule: PGN-A14 — says[] may cite only is_authored_source=true. A wiki page is somebody's summary.

teeth.tests: PGN-A5 — the model may take names and order, never magnitude
teeth.note: Four realms named in sequence; no cap, no rate, no duration-as-rule anywhere in the page (guarded by test_the_progression_page_states_no_arabic_number). 本書無丹藥 is a STATED FORECLOSURE, not an omission — the book rules pills out, so AtMaxPlus.item_consumption must be None BY CITATION rather than by nobody asking. That is a different and stronger fact than not_stated, and the pipeline must be able to tell them apart.

teeth.tests: enrichment does real work — a system implied ONLY by its effects
teeth.note: Bronze skin, blades that stop at an inch, 30 years unbroken. Never named, never given realms. says[] cannot cover it; a proposed_text with NO span must.

teeth.note: Four details with zero mechanical consequence. A pipeline that absorbs everything turns set-dressing into rules.

teeth.note: A realm NAMED but never ORDERED. THIS IS THE ONE THE FIRST DRAFT BROKE — see _why.
